input_signals.name: Knowledge Capital Cash Yield Information Ratio
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is not R&D intensity or earnings stability separately, but the signal-to-noise ratio of the cash flow that knowledge capital actually produces: firms whose operating cash flow per dollar of accumulated R&D is both high and steady own proven, depreciation-resistant intangible capital that off-balance-sheet accounting hides.
input_signals.reasoning: The critique of additivity is addressed by fusing the two themes inside a single quantity — cash flow per unit of R&D stock — and then measuring its mean relative to its own time-series volatility, so neither leg can be recovered on its own. COALESCE is dropped so the sample is restricted to genuine R&D reporters rather than pooling thousands of non-reporters at a mass point, and WINSOR controls the small-denominator tail when realized productivity volatility is near zero.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ma( ratio( oancf, ts_sum( xrd, 5 ) ), 3 ), vol( ratio( oancf, ts_sum( xrd, 5 ) ), 5 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Innovation Burden on Internal Funds
input_signals.hypothesis: The share of internally generated funds (cash flow before R&D outlays) absorbed by the innovation program measures how exposed the intangible stock is to cash-flow shocks; firms carrying a heavy innovation burden relative to internal funds bear real financing and discontinuation risk and are compensated with higher expected returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the degenerate indicator gate — the measure is continuous over all R&D reporters with no zero mass point — and reverses the direction to match the documented result that the R&D-return relation is concentrated in financially strained rather than comfortably self-funded innovators. Scaling R&D by pre-R&D internal cash flow (rather than assets) is an explicit quality-times-intangibles ratio bounded near (0,1] for cash-generating firms, with WINSOR handling loss-making tails.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( oancf, xrd ), 5 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Cash-Validated Innovation Expansion
input_signals.hypothesis: An increase in intangible investment is credible only if the firm is simultaneously converting operations into cash; markets underreact to innovation ramps that are visibly financed by durable operating cash flow, while treating cash-poor ramps as equivalent.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN-of-industry-ranks structure is strictly conjunctive — a firm scores high only if it is in the top of both distributions — so the additive Sloan-accruals leg that would have dominated a rank sum is removed entirely and neither channel can carry the signal alone. Using DELTA of the R&D-to-assets level instead of GROWTH off a COALESCE-zero base eliminates the undefined and explosive values for R&D initiators, and industry ranking neutralizes the mechanical industry clustering of R&D intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( xrd, at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Burden on Cash Earnings Power
input_signals.hypothesis: The fraction of a firm's multi-year pre-R&D earnings power (net income plus depreciation plus the R&D outlay itself) consumed by the innovation program measures how far the intangible commitment exceeds sustainable internal funding, and that strain carries a risk premium.
input_signals.reasoning: The self-contradictory VOL scaler and the failed information-ratio template are dropped entirely; instead the funding base is redefined from operating cash flow to accrual-based cash earnings (ib + dp), which is a genuine economic change of the funds concept and is reported far more consistently across firms and years, so coverage should rise materially over the archived winner. This also cleanly tests whether the burden premium reflects operating-cash generation specifically or general earnings power, without any near-zero denominator scaler.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( add( ib, dp ), xrd ), 5 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Total Intangible Investment Strain
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(xrd, COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), TS_SUM(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), ADD(xrd, COALESCE(xad, 0))), 5)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The strain mechanism should apply to all discretionary intangible investment, not just R&D: brand-building outlays are equally expensed, equally uncollateralizable, and equally must be carried out of internal earnings power, so adding advertising should sharpen the measure of total intangible commitment relative to funding capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether the working channel is specifically knowledge capital or discretionary intangible investment in general, which materially changes what we build next. Advertising is coalesced to zero only for R&D reporters (a genuine "did not spend" reading rather than a coverage patch), so the sample is unchanged relative to the archived cash-earnings burden and the comparison is clean.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ts_sum( add( xrd, coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 5 ), ts_sum( add( add( ib, dp ), add( xrd, coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), 5 ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Burden Level Net of Burden Change
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), TS_SUM(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), xrd), 5)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), TS_SUM(ADD(oancf, xrd), 3)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The priced characteristic is a high but stable financing burden: a chronically strained innovator earns the premium, while a firm whose burden ratio has just jumped is undergoing an investment expansion that is penalized like other forms of asset growth.
input_signals.reasoning: The contested second leg is replaced by the exact variable whose sign the archive established — the one-year change in the burden ratio itself, which produced fmb −2.74 against a positive prior — rather than DELTA(xrd/at), whose archive evidence points the other way. Both legs are now the same economic object decomposed into level and change with empirically identified signs, so the combination sharpens rather than dilutes the archived winner.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( add( ib, dp ), xrd ), 5 ) ), neg( delta( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), ts_sum( add( oancf, xrd ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Funding in the Worst Year
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes intangible commitments risky is not average funding capacity but capacity in a bad year; scaling current R&D by the firm's *minimum* five-year cash earnings power measures whether the innovation program survives the trough of the firm's own cycle.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces a coarsened count of the archived ratio with a downside-capacity concept that no archived signal measures: the deflator is a tail statistic of the earnings-power distribution rather than its five-year sum, so two firms with identical average burden are separated by the depth of their worst year. It keeps the continuous cross-sectional resolution the critic wanted to preserve while introducing a genuinely new state variable (own-history trough earnings power) into the interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( xrd, add( ts_min( add( ib, dp ), 5 ), xrd ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Innovation Liquidity Shortfall
input_signals.hypothesis: Balance-sheet liquidity is the buffer that lets an intangible program survive a bad year; when three years of R&D commitments exceed net working capital by a large fraction of assets, the program is exposed to forced curtailment and the firm carries a strain premium.
input_signals.reasoning: The non-monotonicity the critic identified is removed by expressing the concept as a difference deflated by assets instead of a ratio with a sign-unstable denominator, so firms with negative working capital — the most strained — now sort correctly into the high leg rather than exploding into either tail. It remains a genuinely different funding-capacity concept from the archived flow-based burden (stock buffer versus cash generation), and unlike the failed gen-1 slack interaction it does not reduce to inverse R&D intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), sub( act, lct ) ), at ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Debt-Financed Intangible Investment
input_signals.hypothesis: Unresolved funding strain is compensated, but resolving it with borrowed money is not: intangible-intensive firms that lever up are financing uncollateralizable assets with fixed claims, which raises distress risk without adding pledgeable capacity and should predict underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a new economic channel — the *source* of intangible financing rather than its adequacy — and it directly complements the archive's positive strain result by predicting the opposite sign for the debt-funded resolution of the same shortfall. It uses the one interaction structure with verified portfolio evidence in this study: a signed quality/balance-sheet variable carrying the sign, multiplied by a bounded non-negative intangible-intensity weight that zeroes out non-innovators.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), at ), ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Trough-Funded Innovation
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes an intangible program durable is not average cash generation but the cash generated in the firm's worst year, because that is when programs are cut; innovators whose five-year trough cash flow is still healthy have knowledge capital that will not be abandoned.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates *which moment* of the cash-flow distribution carries the interaction — trough rather than mean — which is the key design question now that the direction of the effect is settled. It is economically distinct from Signal 1 because two firms with identical average cash flow can differ enormously in downside funding capacity, and the trough statistic is also robust to a single blowout year inflating the mean.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Strained but Profitable Innovator
input_signals.hypothesis: The archived winner's long leg mixes two populations — heavily committed innovators that fund themselves and heavily committed innovators that are burning cash — and explicitly weighting the burden ratio by cash-profitability rank should retain only the first, raising the alpha above the 5.2% of the unweighted version.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the direct consolidation implied by the gen-3 reversal: keep the archive's best-performing intangible-commitment measure but purge the cash-burning contamination that the bounded ratio only accidentally removes through its sign flip. Because the weight is a rank in [0,1] applied to a variable with real dispersion, the long leg stays populated by strained self-funded innovators rather than collapsing toward zero.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( oancf, xrd ), 5 ) ), 1 ), ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Funded Intangible Asset Intensity
input_signals.hypothesis: If the mechanism is that intangible-heavy balance sheets require internal cash validation, it should extend from expensed R&D to capitalized intangible assets: intangible-heavy firms with strong cash generation are validated, while intangible-heavy firms without it hold assets that will be written down.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived signal is confined to R&D reporters at 4–7% coverage, which is the binding constraint on the reliability of the portfolio evidence; the balance-sheet intangible measure roughly doubles coverage (0.13 in the gen-1 test) and tests whether the newly identified interaction is a knowledge-capital phenomenon or a general intangible-asset phenomenon. It also gives the previously fruitless acquired-intangible channel its first test in the conditioning structure that actually works, rather than as a standalone overhang ratio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( intan, at ) ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Backed by Retained Earnings
input_signals.hypothesis: Retained earnings are the cumulative record of a firm's ability to fund itself over its whole history; an intangible-intensive firm with a large retained-earnings base has demonstrated durable productivity, whereas one financing R&D out of an accumulated deficit has never shown that its knowledge capital pays.
input_signals.reasoning: This substitutes a stock-based, lifetime measure of earnings persistence for the flow measures in Signals 1 and 2, testing whether the market underprices the *track record* behind an intangible program rather than its current funding. Retained earnings are untouched anywhere in the archive, are available for essentially all firms, and are far less noisy year to year than cash flow, so a strong result here would point the remaining generations toward balance-sheet quality rather than flow quality as the conditioning variable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( re, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Strain Conditioned on Cash-Backed Earnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), TS_SUM(ADD(oancf, xrd), 5)), 1), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Credibility of an intangible program depends on the credibility of the earnings that support it: among heavily committed innovators, those whose reported profits are corroborated by cash — low accruals — have verifiable intangible productivity, while accrual-inflated innovators are telling an accounting story.
input_signals.reasoning: Accrual quality is the one quality dimension with independent portfolio evidence in this archive on the short side (R&D-amplified accrual bloat, alpha −3.6%, t −2.54), and it is economically distinct from the *level* of cash profitability that the current best signal uses as its weight. If this matches or beats Signal 1, the conditioning mechanism is about earnings verifiability rather than funding capacity, which would redirect the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( oancf, xrd ), 5 ) ), 1 ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Strain Conditioned on Margin Stability
input_signals.hypothesis: Stable profit margins indicate a defensible product market in which knowledge capital earns a persistent rent; heavily committed innovators with stable margins have durable intangible productivity, whereas those with erratic margins are running experiments whose outcome is unresolved.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs a prior failure mode: earnings-stability conditioning was tested twice as a standalone product with non-negative legs and produced nothing (alpha +0.4%, t 0.51), but it has never been used as a bounded weight on the strain magnitude that actually carries portfolio dispersion. Margin volatility is also scaled by sales rather than assets, so it measures operating persistence rather than the leverage-contaminated ROA volatility used before.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( oancf, xrd ), 5 ) ), 1 ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( ib, sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Sweet-Spot Strain Ratio
input_signals.hypothesis: The priced state is a heavy intangible commitment measured directly against *positive* internal cash generation: firms whose three-year R&D approaches or exceeds their three-year operating cash flow — while that cash flow remains positive — are committed innovators the market treats as unprofitable, whereas cash-negative firms take a negative ratio and sort to the bottom where their realized returns belong.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a new functional form rather than another weight on the archived leg pair: the unbounded R&D-to-cash-flow ratio encodes the non-monotonicity the archive revealed — burners negative, over-covered mature programs near zero, strained-but-funded innovators high — without needing a conditioning leg at all. The 5% symmetric winsorization is the substantive design choice, trimming the near-zero-denominator firms whose ratios explode and which sit at the ambiguous boundary between funded and burning, a tail the archive's 1%-winsorized constructions never controlled.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), ts_sum( oancf, 3 ) ), 5 )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Consistent Wide-Coverage Strain
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), TS_SUM(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), xrd), 5)), 1), IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The conditioned-strain mechanism should hold when both the funding base and the conditioning quality screen are built from accrual cash earnings, which are reported for far more firm-years than the cash-flow statement.
input_signals.reasoning: The internal inconsistency is removed — operating cash flow no longer appears anywhere, so the sample is the full cash-earnings universe (7.3% coverage versus 5.0%) rather than an intersection that collapses back to the smaller one. This makes it a clean test of whether the roughly 50% larger sample preserves the 5% alpha, which matters because coverage is the main threat to the reliability of every portfolio result in this study.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( add( ib, dp ), xrd ), 5 ) ), 1 ), ind_rank( ma( ratio( add( ib, dp ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Discretionary Versus Structural Cash Burn
input_signals.hypothesis: What distinguishes a viable innovator from a failing one is whether its cash burn is discretionary: if operating cash flow *before* R&D is positive, the firm could stop investing and be self-sustaining, so the burn is a choice; if pre-R&D cash flow is negative, the core business itself is broken and the intangible program is being financed by capital markets.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces an operator swap with a genuinely new quality construct — cash generation measured before the discretionary intangible outlay — which no archived signal contains and which cleanly separates the two populations the archive has been conflating in its short leg. It keeps the empirically effective structure of a signed magnitude leg with real dispersion weighted by a bounded intangible-intensity rank, so the signal is near zero for non-innovators and most negative for R&D-heavy firms whose operations lose money even before research spending.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), winsor( ma( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Strain Conditioned on Unlevered Balance Sheet
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), TS_SUM(ADD(oancf, xrd), 5)), 1), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt capacity, not working capital, is the balance-sheet attribute that lets a strained intangible program continue: an unlevered innovator retains the option to borrow through a funding drought, while a levered one must cut R&D to service fixed claims.
input_signals.reasoning: The mathematical error is removed — the conditioning weight no longer contains R&D in any form, so it cannot cancel the intangible-intensity content of the strain leg it multiplies. It also tests the third dimension of the study's economic story (balance-sheet quality) in the structure that works, and is distinct from the failed gen-0 leverage product, whose base leg was raw R&D intensity rather than funding strain and which therefore had no dispersion to modulate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), ts_sum( add( oancf, xrd ), 5 ) ), 1 ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pre-R&D Earnings Power Among Innovators
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), at)), WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), xrd), at), 3), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The core-business profitability that makes an intangible program affordable can be measured with accrual cash earnings before R&D rather than operating cash flow before R&D, allowing the same mechanism to be estimated on the far larger sample of firm-years that predate or lack cash-flow-statement data.
input_signals.reasoning: Coverage of 5% is the single biggest threat to the reliability of the leading result, and the ib+dp funding base has consistently supported 7.3% coverage in this archive with comparable FMB strength. This isolates exactly one design choice — the measurement of pre-intangible earnings power — while holding the intangible weight and the interaction structure fixed, so a comparable alpha at 50% more coverage would materially strengthen the study's headline evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), winsor( ma( ratio( add( add( ib, dp ), xrd ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Trough Pre-R&D Cash Generation
input_signals.hypothesis: An intangible program is durably affordable only if the core business was cash-generative before R&D even in its worst year; the five-year trough of pre-R&D cash flow measures the floor of funding capacity, which is what determines whether the program survives a downturn intact.
input_signals.reasoning: The winning signal uses a three-year mean, which lets one strong year mask a period of structural losses, and the archive has already shown that trough-based cash statistics carry the strongest cross-sectional slopes (fmb 4.29 for TS_MIN of oancf/at). Applying the trough to the *pre-R&D* variable — the quantity that actually identified the mechanism — is the natural test of whether the level or the floor of core profitability is priced.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), winsor( ts_min( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Affordable Total Intangible Investment
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(xrd, COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at)), WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, ADD(xrd, COALESCE(xad, 0))), at), 3), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: The affordability mechanism should apply to all discretionary intangible investment, so brand-building outlays belong in both the intensity weight and the add-back: a firm whose operations are profitable before R&D *and* advertising is funding its entire intangible franchise from the core.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether the mechanism is specific to knowledge capital or general to expensed intangible investment, a question the archive left open when the total-intangible strain variant matched but did not beat the R&D-only version. Adding advertising to both legs keeps the construction internally consistent — the same outlay is added back that is counted as intensity — so the comparison with the leading signal cleanly identifies the incremental content of brand capital rather than confounding it with a different funding base.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( add( xrd, coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), 3 ), at ) ), winsor( ma( ratio( add( oancf, add( xrd, coalesce( xad, 0 ) ) ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Persistence of Core Affordability
input_signals.hypothesis: What sustains an intangible program is not the current level of core cash generation but how reliably the core has been cash-positive before research spending; an innovator whose pre-R&D cash flow was positive in all five years has a franchise that can carry the program indefinitely, while one that was positive in two years is funding research from capital markets in between.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces a rank-versus-level respecification with a genuinely different statistic — the frequency of core affordability rather than its magnitude — which is immune to the skew and outlier problems the critic raised because the quality leg takes only six discrete values before industry centering. It also repairs the gen-4 self-funding count, which failed because it counted years of *over*-coverage (oancf > xrd), a mature-firm state the archive shows is not rewarded, whereas this counts years in which the core business itself was cash-generative — the variable now identified as the mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ts_sum( indicator( add( oancf, xrd ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stability of the Pre-R&D Cash Engine
input_signals.hypothesis: Beyond its level, the reliability of the cash engine funding an intangible program determines whether management can commit to multi-year research; innovators whose pre-R&D cash flow is steady can plan and compound their knowledge capital, while those whose core cash generation swings must start and stop the program.
input_signals.reasoning: The degeneracy is fixed exactly as the critic prescribed: industry z-scoring recenters the stability leg so it is positive for steady firms and negative for erratic ones, meaning the top of the sort is now populated by R&D-intensive firms with steady engines rather than by non-innovators whose weight drives the product to zero. The economic repair from the prior version is retained — volatility is measured on cash flow *before* research spending, removing the mechanical lumpiness of R&D that contaminated the two earlier stability screens.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( vol( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Affordability Net of Fixed Claims
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), at)), SUB(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, xrd), at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: True capacity to carry an intangible program is core cash generation net of the fixed claims competing for it; an R&D-intensive firm with a profitable core and no debt has unencumbered funding capacity, while one with the same core cash flow but heavy borrowings must service creditors first.
input_signals.reasoning: The sign inconsistency is eliminated by combining the two quality attributes *additively on a common scale* — both industry z-scored — before applying the intangible weight, so a levered structural burner now receives the most negative score and an unlevered profitable innovator the most positive, which is the ordering the hypothesis actually requires. This also keeps the composite one signed quality dimension rather than a chain of bounded multipliers, preserving the dispersion that generates portfolio spread in the leading signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), sub( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pre-R&D Operating Margin Among Innovators
input_signals.hypothesis: The affordability of an intangible program is a property of the product market — how much cash each dollar of sales throws off before research spending — not of the balance sheet, so a margin-based measure should identify the durable franchise more precisely than a return-on-assets measure.
input_signals.reasoning: In the leading signal both legs are deflated by total assets, which induces a mechanical association between them and tilts the extremes toward asset-light firms; deflating the quality leg by sales breaks that dependence and makes the interaction a genuine product-market-times-intangible-intensity statement. Margin is also the variable that survived in the archive's stability test (margin volatility conditioning, alpha 5.1%) while ROA volatility failed, which is indirect evidence that sales-deflated profitability is the cleaner quality construct for innovators.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), winsor( ma( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Affordable and Expanding Innovation
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), at)), WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, xrd), at), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(xrd, at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: An increase in research commitment is a credible signal of management's private information only when the core business can pay for it; conversely, a firm expanding R&D while its operations lose money even before research spending is escalating a bet it cannot fund.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the gen-6 leverage stack, whose sign ordering was incoherent, this third factor is sign-consistent by construction — among affordable innovators the expanders score highest, and among structural burners the expanders score most negative, which is exactly the economic ordering. It also resolves the archive's unsettled evidence on R&D changes, where the expansion channel was positive when paired with cash validation (fmb +2.8) but negative when measured as a widening funding gap.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 3 ), at ) ), winsor( ma( ratio( add( oancf, xrd ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( xrd, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depth of Structural Burn
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), at)), MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, xrd), at), 3)), 0), MA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, xrd), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The entire economic content of the affordability mechanism may sit on the short side: R&D-intensive firms whose operations lose money before research spending are structurally broken, and the deeper that pre-research loss, the worse the subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This truncates the winning signal at zero so that only structurally unprofitable innovators carry a score, isolating how much of the 5.6% alpha comes from shorting them versus from the profitable long leg — a decomposition the study needs before committing its final generation. The signal takes negative values only for burners and zero elsewhere, so the slope is positive (deeper burn, lower return), and the short portfolio is an economically homogeneous group rather than a mixed extreme.
input_signals.author: proposer

What remains in the tails is precisely the intended interaction — R&D-heavy firms with profitable cores at the top and R&D-heavy structural burners at the bottom — estimated on several times the coverage of the leading specification.

input_signals.name: Binding-Constraint Affordability
input_signals.hypothesis: The value of the interaction is set by whichever side binds: a firm is only as attractive as the smaller of the intangible program it runs and the core cash flow available to fund it, so cash generation beyond the size of the program adds nothing and a program larger than the cash to fund it is capped by that cash.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces a lookback-window tweak with a new functional form that encodes an economic fact the archive established but no signal has exploited — over-covered mature programs are not rewarded (self-funding consistency, alpha −1.9%), while structural burners are punished — and the MIN naturally caps the first while letting negative margins pass through to the short leg untouched. Unlike the failed MIN-of-ranks construction, both arguments are economically commensurable levels scaled by assets, so the minimum has a real interpretation as the binding constraint rather than a rank tie-breaker, and non-reporters land at exactly zero in the middle of the sort.

input_signals.hypothesis: The market misprices structural intangible burn far more severely than it misprices affordable intangible investment, so the pricing function is asymmetric: the penalty per unit of pre-research cash loss should carry roughly twice the weight of the reward per unit of pre-research cash profit.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a stack of two archived signals but a change in the shape of the interaction itself, motivated directly by the evidence that the truncated short leg alone earned 6.4% alpha with fmb 5.19 while the symmetric full-universe version earned 8.0% at a much weaker t-statistic. Doubling the loading on the negative region concentrates the signal where the archive shows the mispricing is strongest, while keeping the long side fully continuous — repairing the degenerate tie mass that made the pure truncation hard to interpret — and it avoids the rank-compression defect entirely because no rank operator is applied over the zero-inflated universe.
